about: The bug hunt's honesty rules, the one copy both ways of hunting read: the walk with no AI (npm run bug-hunt) and the /bug-hunt skill. Taken from Debbie O'Brien's site-bug-hunt skill (debbie.codes), made our own. Noise is worse than silence: a finding nobody can trust costs more than one that was missed.

classifications.bug: The site is broken for a person using it: a server error, a crash, an empty page, a dead link, a wrong answer.
classifications.expected-bad-ux: It works as designed but feels wrong. Only a person or Claude can call this; the walk never does.
classifications.env: The environment, not the site: a network failure, something outside the bank, a local-only problem.
classifications.test-gap: Nothing is broken, but no automated test covers it. Only Claude calls this; the walk never does.
classifications.inconclusive: Suspicious but not confirmed in this run. Prefer this over a guess.

confidence.high: Seen again when the step was repeated in this run.
confidence.medium: Seen once; one thing is still uncertain (the step could not be repeated safely).

severity.blocker: A page crashes or cannot be used at all.
severity.major: A server error (5xx) or an uncaught error in the page.
severity.minor: A console error, a dead link, a security-policy refusal.

fingerprint: <target>|<page or endpoint as a pattern>|<symptom>. The same fingerprint is one finding, however many pages show it.
rules: The local site only (http://127.0.0.1:4173/app), never the live site on Render.
Its own accounts: a fresh customer for anything that changes data; the demo Admin and Support only look.
Practice mode on for its own session only, never anybody else's.
Never read the planted-fault list (GET /api/practice) before or while exploring; only when scoring at the end.
A finding that also happens with practice mode off is new: the planted faults are off then.

A planted fault counts as found only when a finding happened where the fault lives (its endpoint, its page, or the same area) and tells the same story (its words, the rare ones counting most), with that fault clearly ahead of every other there. Each finding finds one fault at most; anything weaker is a maybe, never found.
Never fix a bug (the planted bugs stay) and never file a GitHub issue.
Never write a secret into a finding: values that look like keys, tokens or passwords are masked.
handOff: A new finding classed bug with high confidence is handed to the /bug-report skill, which keeps the local bug records.
